direct_answer: Gain staging is the management of level at every handoff, not a single target on one meter. Map where gain changes before solving the symptom. Treat numeric levels as context and evidence, not a universal recipe.
evidence_needed: The exact source, bus, output, plug-in order, meter position, and current Logic version.
A matched before/after comparison using the same representative musical section.
Input, output, gain-reduction, peak, true-peak, RMS/LUFS, and routing evidence only where relevant.
The user’s report of what became cleaner, louder, denser, flatter, harsher, punchier, quieter, or more cohesive.
key_distinction: Gain staging is the management of level at every handoff, not a single target on one meter. Map where gain changes before solving the symptom.
limitations: Numeric levels, headroom values, bus settings, ceilings, and loudness readings are orientations or measurements, not universal presets.
Meters describe signal behavior; they do not prove artistic improvement.
Analog-modeled plug-ins use product-specific calibration and nonlinear behavior.
Professional and community sources are context-bound and may disagree.
Exact Logic procedures remain unverified on the owner’s installed build.

logic_guidance.listen_for: the first point where level, tone, noise, or dynamics diverge from the intended chain
logic_guidance.location: Logic Mixer > source channel > inserts > fader > bus/aux > Stereo Out
logic_guidance.risk: Changing several stages at once can hide the true overload or under-drive point.
logic_guidance.show_me_query: Logic Mixer > source channel > inserts > fader > bus/aux > Stereo Out
logic_guidance.starting_point: Keep the fader position unchanged while using meters or a temporary Gain plug-in to identify the first stage that becomes unexpectedly hot or quiet.
steps: Save or document the current routing, gain, processor, fader, meter, and automation state before the experiment.
Bypass nothing; play the loudest representative section and inspect one stage at a time from region/source through inserts, fader, buses, and output.
Use the same representative passage and match perceived output loudness before judging tone, dynamics, punch, or cohesion.
Listen for: the first point where level, tone, noise, or dynamics diverge from the intended chain.

Remove the temporary meter/Gain instance and restore the documented starting values.
logic_guidance.stop_condition: Stop once you can repeatably hear the first point where level, tone, noise, or dynamics diverge from the intended chain in the full context. Back off or undo if Changing several stages at once can hide the true overload or under-drive point.
logic_guidance.undo: Remove the temporary meter/Gain instance and restore the documented starting values.
